summary: An exceptionally busy week. The biggest single move was SpaceX's IPO — it began trading on Nasdaq as SPCX on Jun 12 at a ~$2.1T valuation, the largest IPO in history. Biology delivered two genetic-medicine firsts: Intellia's lonvo-z became the first in vivo CRISPR therapy to win a positive pivotal Phase 3 (hereditary angioedema, 87% attack reduction, NEJM), and Prime Medicine secured the first-ever clinical authorization for an in vivo prime editor (PM577a, Wilson Disease) — alongside a 9-0 FDA adcomm for Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine and an independent at-home ALS speech BCI in Nature Medicine. In AI, Z.ai's open-weight GLM-5.2 became the first open model past 80% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, Google shipped the open text-diffusion DiffusionGemma, and 'world models, not LLM scaling, for embodied intelligence' emerged as the week's dominant cross-voice thesis (Jim Fan, LeCun, Fei-Fei Li), with NVIDIA's DreamZero as its falsifiable evidence and NYU/DeepMind's Sherry Yang added as a new voice. On the physical side, QuEra+AWS announced a 256-logical-qubit fault-tolerant system ('Libra') for 2028 and QuantumScape signed Honda as its second solid-state OEM. Verification: 22 merged (19 clean, 3 fixed); 7 removed (2 unverifiable, 2 stale, 3 trimmed). Entities: 3 untracked players added (Z.ai, QuantumScape, Autolus).

highlights.title: GLM-5.2: first open-weight model past 80% on Terminal-Bench 2.1
highlights.detail: Z.ai released GLM-5.2 (744B-param MoE, 40B active, 1M context, MIT license) in mid-June 2026; reported as the first open-weight model to cross 80% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (81.0) and 62.1 on SWE-bench Pro, beating GPT-5.5 (58.6) at roughly 1/6th the cost.

payload.claim: Open-weight frontier coding/agentic model GLM-5.2 (744B MoE, MIT, 1M context) becomes first open model >80% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (81.0) and 62.1 SWE-bench Pro, beating GPT-5.5 at ~1/6 cost.

highlights.title: IndexShare: shared sparse-attention indexer cuts per-token FLOPs 2.9x at 1M ctx
highlights.detail: GLM-5.2 introduces IndexShare, reusing one indexer across every four sparse-attention layers to cut per-token FLOPs by 2.9x at 1M-token context — an attention-efficiency technique enabling cheap long-horizon agentic coding in an open-weight model.

payload.name: IndexShare shared sparse-attention indexer
payload.description: A sparse-attention efficiency method that reuses a single indexer across groups of four attention layers, reducing per-token FLOPs by 2.9x at 1M context, demonstrated at frontier quality in GLM-5.2.
examples: GLM-5.2 (Z.ai, June 2026): 2.9x per-token FLOP reduction at 1M context via IndexShare

highlights.title: DiffusionGemma: Google open-weight text-diffusion LLM, 1000+ tok/s on one H100
highlights.detail: Google DeepMind released DiffusionGemma (2026-06-10), a 26B-A4B MoE text-diffusion model (3.8B active) under Apache 2.0 that denoises a 256-token canvas in parallel for up to 4x faster generation (1000+ tok/s on one H100), with bidirectional self-correction and vLLM support.

payload.claim: Google's DiffusionGemma (26B-A4B MoE, Apache 2.0, 2026-06-10) is an open-weight discrete-diffusion language model that generates 256-token canvases in parallel for up to 4x faster decoding (1000+ tok/s on one H100) with bidirectional self-correction.

highlights.title: Stellantis + Wayve + Uber sign MoU to scale L4 robotaxis globally
highlights.detail: On 2026-06-17 Stellantis, Wayve and Uber signed a non-binding MoU to develop and deploy Level-4 robotaxis at global scale, pairing Stellantis 'L4-Ready Platforms', Wayve's mapless end-to-end AI Driver, and Uber's network across Europe and North America.

payload.name: Stellantis x Wayve x Uber L4 robotaxi partnership
payload.why: Three-way ecosystem (OEM platform + mapless embodied-AI driver + global ride network) to mass-produce and deploy L4 robotaxis without city-by-city mapping; signals convergence on Wayve's end-to-end approach.
payload.funding: Non-binding MoU; no financial terms disclosed

highlights.title: Test-time-compute scaling fails for long-horizon coding agents; representation is the bottleneck
highlights.detail: arxiv 2604.16529 ('Scaling Test-Time Compute for Agentic Coding', Kim et al., incl. Salakhutdinov/Synnaeve) reports standard test-time scaling (parallel sampling/best-of-N) does not transfer cleanly to long-horizon agents, identifying how to represent and reuse prior experience — not raw compute — as the central bottleneck. Surging on arxiv/alphaXiv.

payload.claim: For long-horizon agentic coding, standard test-time compute scaling does not transfer cleanly; the central bottleneck is representing and reusing prior agent experience rather than adding inference compute.

highlights.title: MCP statelessness lands in 2026-07-28 spec RC; Claude gets enterprise-managed MCP + sandboxed agents
highlights.detail: MCP statelessness changes landed in the MCP 2026-07-28 release candidate (published May 2026); Anthropic added enterprise-managed MCP connectors (Okta first, zero-touch on first login) and self-hosted sandboxes plus MCP tunnels that let managed agents reach private MCP servers.

payload.field: MCP protocol + enterprise agent primitives status (mid-2026)
payload.new_value: MCP statelessness in the 2026-07-28 spec RC (published May 2026); Anthropic adds enterprise-managed MCP connectors (Okta first) and self-hosted sandboxes + MCP tunnels for private MCP server access from managed agents
payload.previous_value: Stateful MCP; no centralized enterprise connector provisioning; no sandboxed managed-agent access to private MCP servers

highlights.title: Intellia lonvo-z: first positive pivotal Phase 3 for in vivo CRISPR (HAE), NEJM
highlights.detail: At EAACI 2026 (Jun 13, 2026) and published in NEJM, Intellia's lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z), a single-dose LNP-delivered CRISPR therapy inactivating KLKB1 in the liver, cut mean monthly hereditary-angioedema attacks by 87% vs placebo (p<0.0001) with 62% of patients attack-free over 6 months (vs 11% placebo) — the first positive pivotal Phase 3 for an in vivo CRISPR therapy; rolling BLA targeting 1H 2027.

payload.claim: Intellia's lonvo-z became the first in vivo CRISPR therapy to win a positive pivotal Phase 3 (HAELO), cutting hereditary angioedema attacks 87% vs placebo (p<0.0001) with 62% attack-free over 6 months; NEJM-published, rolling BLA underway for 1H 2027 launch.

highlights.title: First in vivo prime editing trial cleared: Prime Medicine PM577a for Wilson Disease
highlights.detail: On Jun 18, 2026, Prime Medicine (Nasdaq: PRME) said New Zealand Medsafe cleared the CTA for PM577a, an LNP-delivered in vivo Prime Editor correcting the ATP7B H1069Q mutation in Wilson Disease — the first clinical authorization for an in vivo prime editing therapy; global Phase 1/2 starts 2H 2026.

payload.name: In vivo prime editing reaches the clinic
payload.description: Prime Medicine's PM577a, an LNP-formulated prime editor delivered IV to hepatocytes, is the first in vivo prime editing therapy authorized for human trials, correcting the ATP7B H1069Q mutation in Wilson Disease.

highlights.title: CAR-T for lupus: Autolus obe-cel CARLYSLE Phase 1 data at EULAR 2026
highlights.detail: At EULAR 2026 (announced Jun 12, 2026 by UCL/UCLH), Autolus' fast-off-rate CD19 CAR-T obecabtagene autoleucel (obe-cel) showed that among 6 patients at the 50M target dose, 5/6 (83%) achieved remission per standard lupus criteria, with several reaching complete or partial renal responses, in severe refractory systemic lupus, with a favorable safety profile.

payload.claim: Autolus' fast-off-rate CD19 CAR-T obe-cel showed 83% (5/6) remission (per standard lupus criteria) at target dose, with several complete/partial renal responses, in severe refractory lupus in the Phase 1 CARLYSLE trial, presented at EULAR 2026.

highlights.title: EvolutionaryScale/CZ Biohub protein LM beats AF-class on complexes; maps 6.8B sequences
highlights.detail: A bioRxiv preprint (early June 2026) from Alexander Rives and the EvolutionaryScale/CZ Biohub team reports a protein language model that exceeds established methods on biomolecular complex / antibody-antigen prediction, designs nanomolar binders via simple search, and maps 6.8B sequences with 1.1B predicted structures.

payload.claim: A new protein language model from EvolutionaryScale/CZ Biohub (Rives et al., bioRxiv Jun 2026) beats established methods on biomolecular complex/antibody-antigen structure prediction, designs nanomolar miniprotein and single-chain antibody binders via simple search, and maps 6.8B sequences with 1.1B predicted structures.

highlights.title: Independent at-home speech+cursor BCI for ALS patient (UC Davis, Nature Medicine)
highlights.detail: A Nature Medicine paper (published 15 June 2026) from UC Davis with Mass General Brigham reports a man with ALS using an intracortical BCI independently at home (3,800+ hours, without researcher support) for both speech-to-text (averaging 56 words/min) and cursor control — a key step from lab demo to durable self-administered assistive tech.

payload.claim: A UC Davis-led intracortical BCI (Nature Medicine, 15 June 2026) enabled a man with ALS to communicate independently at home via speech-to-text (averaging 56 words/min) and cursor control without researcher support over 3,800+ hours, demonstrating long-term self-administered use.

highlights.title: FDA adcomm votes 9-0 for Moderna's mRNA seasonal flu vaccine (mFluvisa)
highlights.detail: On Jun 18, 2026, the FDA's VRBPAC voted unanimously (9-0) in favor of Moderna's mRNA seasonal influenza vaccine (mRNA-1010, brand mFluvisa), backing full approval for adults 50-64 and accelerated approval for 65+ — the first mRNA-based seasonal flu vaccine to reach an FDA adcomm; decision expected Aug 5, 2026.

payload.field: mRNA seasonal flu vaccine regulatory status
payload.new_value: FDA VRBPAC voted 9-0 (Jun 18, 2026) for Moderna's mRNA-1010 (mFluvisa) seasonal flu vaccine (full approval 50-64; accelerated approval 65+); FDA decision expected Aug 5, 2026
payload.previous_value: mRNA flu vaccines still investigational; FDA refusal-to-file on Moderna's application in Feb 2026

highlights.title: QuEra + AWS unveil 'Libra' 256-logical-qubit fault-tolerant system for 2028
highlights.detail: On 2026-06-15 AWS and QuEra announced Libra, a neutral-atom machine targeting over 256 error-corrected logical qubits, a 1e-6 logical error rate, and ~1M reliable logical operations, available via Amazon Braket by 2028.

payload.new_value: Libra: 256+ logical qubits, 1e-6 logical error rate, ~1M logical ops, on AWS Braket by 2028
payload.previous_value: QuEra neutral-atom roadmap with no committed fault-tolerant cloud system; Aquila 256-qubit analog Rydberg on Braket since 2022

highlights.title: SpaceX completes IPO; SPCX debuts on Nasdaq at a ~$2.1T valuation
highlights.detail: SpaceX priced its IPO on 2026-06-11 (555,555,555 shares @ $135) and began trading on Nasdaq under 'SPCX' on 2026-06-12, closing up ~19% at ~$161 for a roughly $2.1T valuation — the biggest IPO in history.

payload.new_value: Public company (Nasdaq: SPCX) as of 2026-06-12; IPO priced $135/share, closed ~$161 (+19%), ~$2.1T valuation at first close (largest IPO ever)

highlights.title: QuantumScape signs Honda as second OEM for solid-state batteries
highlights.detail: On 2026-06-18 QuantumScape (NYSE: QS) announced a multi-year joint research/development agreement with Honda R&D for its solid-state lithium-metal platform, following Honda's completion of a technology evaluation; Honda is QS's second major OEM after Volkswagen/PowerCo.

payload.new_value: Honda R&D added as second major OEM (multi-year joint development on solid-state lithium-metal cells & manufacturing), 2026-06-18

highlights.title: D-Wave pivots to dual-rail gate-model FT roadmap (100 logical qubits by 2032)
highlights.detail: On 2026-06-01 D-Wave (NYSE: QBTS), historically an annealing company, unveiled a superconducting gate-model fault-tolerant roadmap built on high-coherence dual-rail qubits (from its Jan-2026 acquisition of Quantum Circuits Inc.), targeting 10 logical qubits by 2030 and 100 logical qubits by 2032.

payload.name: Dual-rail superconducting qubits for fault tolerance
payload.description: Erasure-biased dual-rail encoding (photon-loss/leakage detected as erasures) in superconducting circuits, now pursued by D-Wave via its Quantum Circuits Inc. acquisition as a lower-overhead route to logical qubits, distinct from transmon surface-code approaches.
examples: D-Wave gate-model roadmap: 17 physical qubits 2026 -> 181 by 2028 -> 10 logical 2030 -> 100 logical 2032
Built on Quantum Circuits Inc. dual-rail tech (acquired Jan 2026)

highlights.title: Helion raises $465M Series G at $15.5B valuation
highlights.detail: On 2026-06-04 Helion Energy closed a $465M Series G led by Thrive Capital (with Lux, Lightspeed, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and others) at a $15.5B post-money valuation, bringing total raised to ~$1.5B as it builds its Polaris/Orion path to electricity.

highlights.title: Snap ships standalone Specs AR glasses ($2,195) — spatial-computing bet
highlights.detail: On June 16 2026 Snap unveiled consumer Specs (announced at AWE): standalone AR glasses with two Snapdragon chips and a Niantic Spatial VPS-powered shared world map, shipping Fall 2026 in the US/UK/France; CEO Spiegel framed them as a post-smartphone computer.

payload.detail: Snap's June 16 2026 launch of standalone consumer Specs AR glasses ($2,195, Fall 2026 ship) with Niantic Spatial VPS integration marks a major spatial-computing push against Meta Ray-Ban Display.

highlights.title: World models, not LLM scaling, are the path to physical/embodied intelligence
highlights.detail: A thesis surging across independent voices: pre-train on physical-world dynamics (a la transformers for text) to get embodied generalization. Jim Fan's 'Great Parallel,' LeCun's $1.03B AMI Labs (JEPA), Fei-Fei Li's World Labs, and NVIDIA's open Cosmos 3 all push it; a June 18 Fusion Fund critique argues the physical world has no 'universal token' so the analogy may not hold.

payload.thesis: World models that learn physical-world dynamics (rather than next-token LLM scaling) are the route to embodied/robot generalization — 'The Great Parallel' to the transformer revolution — though critics argue the absence of a universal physical 'token' may prevent the same convergence.
examples: Jim Fan (NVIDIA) 'The Great Parallel' thesis; ~$6B into world-model startups in early 2026
Yann LeCun's AMI Labs raises $1.03B (JEPA/world models)
Fei-Fei Li's World Labs building explicit-3D world models; NVIDIA Cosmos 3 open physical-AI omnimodel
Fusion Fund (June 18 2026) counter-analysis: no universal physical token, so competing architectures won't converge like transformers

highlights.title: Agentic AI reaches autonomous end-to-end clinical care (MIRA, AMIE in Nature)
highlights.detail: Eric Topol (June 17 2026) unpacks two new Nature papers: MIRA (Ferber/Kather et al.) ran autonomous end-to-end ED workups across real cases at 87.8% diagnostic accuracy vs 78.1% for board-certified physicians; Google's AMIE managed longitudinal outpatient care non-inferior to 21 PCPs (simulated settings).

payload.claim: Two June 2026 Nature papers show agentic AI doing autonomous, multi-step, end-to-end clinical management at or above board-certified-physician performance in simulated settings — MIRA (ED, 87.8% vs 78.1% dx accuracy) and Google's AMIE (longitudinal outpatient, non-inferior to PCPs).

highlights.title: DreamZero: video-diffusion 'World Action Models' beat VLAs 2x on zero-shot robot tasks
highlights.detail: NVIDIA GEAR's DreamZero (arXiv 2602.15922, 'World Action Models are Zero-shot Policies') is a 14B world-action model on a video-diffusion backbone delivering >2x zero-shot generalization over SOTA VLAs in real-robot tests, with real-time 7Hz closed-loop control and 30-min few-shot embodiment transfer. Surging on HF Papers/alphaXiv as falsifiable evidence behind the world-models-for-robotics thesis (Feb 2026; backfill).

payload.claim: DreamZero (NVIDIA GEAR, 14B World Action Model on a video-diffusion backbone) achieves >2x zero-shot generalization vs state-of-the-art VLAs in real-robot experiments, real-time 7Hz control, and few-shot embodiment transfer in 30 min of play data.

highlights.title: Sherry Yang — generative world models as the substrate for embodied agents
highlights.detail: NYU Courant assistant professor and Google DeepMind staff research scientist anchoring the world-models-for-robotics thesis with primary work: WorldGym (world model as policy-eval environment), World-Gymnast (RL inside a world model improves real-robot VLA policies, Feb 2026), and a position paper 'World Models as an Intermediary between Agents and the Real World.'
